2027-02-17.title: Second Wednesday of the Great Fast
2027-02-17.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Eternal life is the gift of God
2027-02-17.alt: Season of the Great Fast (Sauma Ramba).
2027-02-17.verse: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
theo: The Gospel begins with a group of people we never meet by name. Jesus crosses the lake to his own town, Capernaum, “and just then some people were carrying a paralyzed man lying on a bed.” The man cannot walk to Jesus; others must carry him. Matthew notes something remarkable: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.’” It is the faith of the carriers that Jesus sees. In many of our parishes, during the Great Fast, the priest goes from house to house to hear the confessions of the sick and the elderly and to bring them Holy Communion; in others the young people bring the housebound to church for the penitential service, in wheelchairs, in autorickshaws, sometimes on a chair carried by four. Every such journey repeats this Gospel. Some of us walk to Christ; some of us must be carried; and some of us are called to carry.

Then comes the surprise. The friends had brought the man for his legs, but Jesus speaks first about his sins. The scribes are scandalised: “This man is blaspheming.” Only God can forgive sins, and they are right about that. Jesus answers their unspoken thoughts: “Which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Stand up and walk’? But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins” he said to the paralytic, “Stand up, take your bed and go to your home.” The visible healing proves the invisible one. The deepest paralysis is the one that keeps us from God, and Jesus heals that first. The crowd's response is full of meaning for us: “they glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.” The authority to forgive, which belongs to God alone, Christ has placed in human hands. On Easter evening he will breathe on his apostles and say: “If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them.” Every confession heard in a Kerala parish this Lent stands on this verse.

Paul tells us what forgiveness is for. It is not a licence to go on sinning: “Should we sin because we are not under law but under grace? By no means!” The forgiven are set free, not to belong to nobody, but to belong to God. “For just as you once presented your members as slaves to impurity and to greater and greater iniquity, so now present your members as slaves to righteousness for sanctification.” The man in the Gospel rose and carried the bed that had carried him. So it is with us: the members of our body that once served sin, the hands, the eyes, the tongue, are now to serve holiness. And the end of this road is not wages but a gift: “the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
outline: Ask: who carried you to Christ, and whom are you carrying?
Point 3 · Authority given to human beings
Rise, take up the bed, and serve righteousness.
“Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
live: Offer to bring an elderly or sick person to church, or ask the parish priest to visit someone housebound for confession this Lent.
If you have not yet made your Lenten confession, fix the day now.
Choose one part of your body that has served sin, your eyes, your tongue or your hands, and give it a work of holiness every day this week.
2027-02-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you saw the faith of those who carried the paralysed man and you forgave his sins. Give us friends who carry us to you, and make us friends who carry others. Thank you for giving to human beings the authority to forgive in your name. Raise us from every paralysis of sin, and let us present our members to you for holiness. Glory to you, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Before Holy Communion we pray as sinners who need healing; the Lord who forgave the paralysed man forgives us in the sacrament of reconciliation and feeds us at his table, so that we may rise and walk.

quick: Jesus saw the faith of those who carried the paralysed man.
He healed the deepest paralysis first: your sins are forgiven.
God has given human beings authority to forgive in Christ's name.
2027-02-17.action: Carry someone to Christ today: a visit, a phone call, an offer of a ride to church.
2027-02-17.question: Am I being carried, or am I carrying someone, or am I standing at a distance?

family.explain: Some friends carried a man who could not walk to Jesus. Jesus saw how much they believed, and he said to the man: your sins are forgiven. Then he said: stand up and walk home. Jesus can heal our bodies, and even more, he can heal our hearts. In confession he still says to us: your sins are forgiven.
family.intention: We pray for the sick and elderly people in our parish who cannot come to church.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we could visit or help to come to church this Lent?”

illus: In a parish near Changanassery an old man who had been paralysed by a stroke had not been to church for three years. During the Great Fast four young men from the parish youth group asked whether they might bring him to the penitential service. They carried him down the steep path from his house in a plastic chair, two on each side, and up the church steps. After his confession he wept, and then he laughed, and said he had not felt so light for years. One of the four said afterwards that they had only carried a chair; the Lord had carried the man.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we come to you carried by one another's faith. Speak your word of pardon over us. Amen.
share: When Jesus saw their faith (Matthew 9:2). Whose faith has carried me in my life?
Your sins are forgiven (Matthew 9:2). What keeps me from the sacrament of reconciliation?
Present your members as slaves to righteousness (Romans 6:19). How can my hands and tongue serve holiness this week?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us and heal us.
interc: For priests, that they may be generous ministers of God's forgiveness this Lent.
For the sick, the paralysed and the housebound.
For young people who serve the elderly and the sick in our parishes.
For those who have stayed away from confession for many years.
For our group, that we may carry one another to Christ.
pm.close: Father, you have given such authority to human beings that sins are forgiven in the name of your Son. Make us a people who carry one another, and raise us to walk in newness of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today some people carry a paralysed man to Jesus. He cannot come by himself. And the Gospel says: when Jesus saw their faith, he said, take heart, son; your sins are forgiven (Matthew 9:2). Their faith carried him.

The friends wanted healing for his legs, but Jesus heals his heart first. The deepest paralysis is sin, which keeps us from God. Then, to show that he has authority to forgive sins, Jesus tells the man: stand up, take your bed and go home (Matthew 9:6). And he does.

The crowd glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings (Matthew 9:8). That authority continues in the Church. When the priest says the words of absolution, it is Christ who says to us: your sins are forgiven.

Saint Paul tells us what the forgiven are to do: present your members as slaves to righteousness for sanctification (Romans 6:19). Let us go to confession this Lent, and let us carry someone else to Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, some friends carried a sick man to Jesus because they believed Jesus could help. Jesus forgave him and made him walk. Who can you help to come closer to Jesus this week?

intro: Theme: “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
Friends who carry, the deepest healing, the authority to forgive given to human beings, and members offered for holiness.

sub: A man who could not come by himself.
Some walk, some are carried, some carry.
q: But Moses' hands grew weary; so they took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side, and the other on the other side; so his hands were steady until the sun set.
Bear one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ.
points.apply: Help one sick or elderly person to receive the sacraments this Lent.

q: Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Take heart, son; your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Fix the day of your Lenten confession.

q: as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.
If you forgive the sins of any, they are forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they are retained.
points.apply: Pray this week for the priests who will hear confessions in your parish.

concl: Jesus sees the faith of those who carry, and he heals the deepest paralysis first.
The authority to forgive is in the Church; let us go, and let us bring others.
2027-02-17.resolve: Make your Lenten confession, and help one other person to make theirs.
